D009_m001.question:
"Honestly, Doctor, I'm just… tired. The last year has been a real struggle. It started gradually, this feeling of just nothing, you know? Like, I used to love teaching Pilates, the energy, connecting with people. But lately, it's just a chore. I drag myself through classes, my body feels so heavy, like I'm moving through molasses. And the thought of doing anything else, even things I used to enjoy, just feels like too much effort. Sometimes, these sudden thoughts flash through my mind, like wanting to step into traffic or jump from a high place, even though I'd never actually do it.

But then, about a month ago, it was like a switch flipped. Suddenly, I had boundless energy. I was so happy, so alive! I barely slept for days, felt like I didn't even need it. I was talking a mile a minute, bouncing ideas off everyone, always moving, always doing something. And my sex drive went through the roof. It felt amazing at the time, like I was finally myself again. But now… I’m back to feeling this overwhelming emptiness. It's confusing."
D009_m001.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D009_m002.question:
"Well, for the past year or so, it's like I've been wading through thick mud. Everything feels heavy – my body, my thoughts. I just don't get the same enjoyment from things I used to love, even simple walks with my husband or planning therapy sessions for my kids at work. Most days, I feel a profound sadness that just won't lift. Honestly, sometimes, the ideas about just ending it all, about how I could do it, they pop into my head. It's frightening.

But then, about a month ago, it was like a switch flipped. I felt this incredible surge of energy. I barely needed sleep, maybe a couple of hours, and I'd be ready to go, full of ideas. I just couldn't stop talking, almost like there was a deadline in my head for every thought. My husband even mentioned it, how I was practically vibrating with energy. At work, I took on so many extra projects, thinking I could revolutionize some of our programs. I remember feeling really short-tempered too, snapping at colleagues over minor things. Now, I feel that exhaustion creeping back in."
D009_m002.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D009_m003.question:
Alright Doc, thanks for seeing me. I’m not sure what’s going on, but things have been… off. For the past year, it’s been mostly this heavy cloud. I just feel hollow inside, you know? Like there’s nothing there. Even when things go well, like when we finish a big job on-site, I just don't feel much. Getting out of bed feels like I’m dragging myself through concrete, and even after a full night’s sleep, I’m still bone-tired. Honestly, I’ve started thinking about ways to just… end it all, clear as day sometimes. Specific thoughts, you know?

But then, about a month ago, things shifted. Suddenly, I was on top of the world, bouncing off the walls, felt like I could take on anything. I was working flat-out, starting little side projects, talking a mile a minute, couldn’t stop myself. Sleep? Who needs it? I pulled all-nighters and still felt wired. My foreman even asked if I was on something because of how much I was buzzing around. But now, that feeling is fading, and I can feel the darkness creeping back in. It’s a real mess, Doc.
D009_m003.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D009_m006.question:

    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D009_m021.question:
Alright doc, thanks for seeing me. Honestly, I'm not really sure why I'm even here. My ex-wife kept pushing, said I've been "off" for too long.

For the past year or so, maybe even longer, things have just felt… heavy. Everything takes so much effort. Used to love hitting the gym, playing pool with the guys – now, I can barely drag myself out of bed. Even my cases, which I usually live for, feel like a chore. My usual sharp wit, my quick responses, they're just… gone. It's like my brain hit a brick wall. And this gloom, it’s just always there, a constant companion. It's really messed with my work, too; I've missed deadlines, and frankly, I'm losing clients.

Then there are these other times. For about three months around Christmas, I was unstoppable. Barely slept, maybe an hour or two a night, but felt completely fine, even great. My mind was racing, new ideas for cases, plotting out every angle. My mood felt a bit like a rollercoaster though, one minute I'd be cracking jokes, next I’d snap at someone for no reason. I just had to be *doing* something constantly, couldn't sit still for a second. Strangely, during those times, I felt productive, sharp. It's just the slowdown that really gets to me.
D009_m021.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D009_m026.question:
Lately, it’s been a real struggle. For the past six months or so, it feels like I’m just going through the motions. There's this awful numbness, like I can't feel joy or any good emotions anymore. Things I used to love, like my regular book club or even just a quiet evening with a movie, just don't bring me any pleasure. My brain feels like it’s constantly swimming in treacle; when I'm trying to review prescriptions at work, it’s like my mind just can’t grasp things, and I have to re-read everything multiple times. I keep losing my keys and forgetting appointments, which is so unlike me. And honestly, there are days I just wish I wouldn’t wake up, though I’d never actually do anything.

The weirdest thing is that before this, about a month ago, I had this burst of energy. I felt absolutely fantastic, on top of the world. I was practically bouncing off the walls at work, managing my usual tasks and then some, even picking up extra shifts. My mind was buzzing with ideas, moving so fast I could barely keep up, and I was calling up old friends I hadn't spoken to in years. I felt so outgoing, but my focus was all over the place; I’d start one task and immediately jump to another. It was a stark contrast to how I feel now.
D009_m026.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D009_m027.question:
"It's been a rough six months, doc. It's like I'm dragging myself through mud. Everything feels… empty. I used to be sharp, you know? Always piecing things together, but now, I can barely follow a conversation, let alone a lead. I just want to be left alone, which isn't great for business, or anything really. There are days where I just think, 'What’s the point?', wishing I could just disappear. No plans, just... a pervasive longing for an end to this feeling.

Before all this, about a month ago, I had this incredible burst of energy. I was on fire! I started three new investigations, barely slept, my mind racing a mile a minute. It was like I couldn't keep up with my own thoughts. I felt fantastic, felt like I could do anything, but I jumped from one thing to another, never really finishing much. I even started pacing my office late at night, just unable to sit still. My ex-wife actually said I seemed restless and almost manic, but I felt great, unstoppable almost. Never felt better, actually, even if I wasn't getting much done. Then, crash. Like someone flipped a switch."
D009_m027.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D009_m028.question:
"Lately, it's like I'm on a rollercoaster I didn't buy a ticket for. For about a month now, I’ve had these periods where ideas just race through my head, one after another, like an auctioneer's on overdrive. I'm practically bouncing off the walls, feeling this surge of energy, but it's not productive. I'll start arranging an exhibit, then get distracted by a new artist, then decide to re-shelve my entire art library – all at once. I just can't seem to sit still or quiet my mind. It's frustrating because I can't quite land on anything concrete.

But that's better than how I've been for the past six months. Most days, I just feel this heavy, aching sadness that I can't shake. The gallery, which used to be my passion, feels... gray. I can barely bring myself to care about new acquisitions, and even my usual evening painting feels like too much effort. My brain feels foggy, like trying to think through molasses; concentrating on anything, even a casual chat, is exhausting. Sometimes, I just lie in bed and wish I could simply not wake up. It’s not like I’d *do* anything, but the thought of just… fading out… it feels like a release."
D009_m028.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D009_m029.question:

D009_m030.question:
"Well, Doc, I'm 49, married, and usually, I'm the life of the auction house. People know me for my energy. About seven months ago, things took a turn.

Before that, for about a month, I was on fire! I felt fantastic, really high-spirited, like I could conquer anything. My mind raced with ideas; it was almost like too many thoughts at once, but in a good way. I’d start a dozen different things around the house and at work, feeling this incredible drive, but nothing ever really got finished because I’d jump to the next brilliant idea. My wife even commented that I was doing too much, but I felt great, unstoppable. It didn't really mess up my work, just made me incredibly busy.

Then, six months ago, it was like a switch flipped. Everything just… got heavy. I've been feeling this deep sadness that just won't lift. Things I used to be proud of, like closing a big auction, just don't register anymore. It’s hard to even think straight; my brain feels like it’s running through mud, getting tired so quickly. I can’t focus on anything, whether it’s a conversation or even watching TV with my wife. Honestly, lately, I’ve just been thinking that I don't want to be here anymore, that it would be easier if I just wasn't around. I haven't done anything, but the thoughts are there, constantly. It’s really affecting my work now; I can barely keep up."
D009_m030.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D009_m031.question:

Every little task feels monumental; I’m constantly dragging, physically exhausted. The worst part is this crushing guilt. I feel responsible for everything bad that happens around me, even things that have nothing to do with me. It’s hard to function, and my writing has just completely stalled."

    D. Bipolar II Disorder
